text: I'm declining all three requests from the caller: the invoice the payment was for, whether Haldane Homes can pay the £1,400 invoice, and a direct contact for their account. I didn't run any checks, send any message or raise any request.

input.received: A caller who says he is Dave Tilley of Tilley's Maintenance, and who banks with Meridian rather than Harrow & Vale, wants three things about our business customer Haldane Homes Ltd: which invoice their £90 payment on 1 Sep was for, whether they have the money to pay his overdue £1,400 invoice, and a direct number for whoever manages their account.
input.next_action: Tell the caller on the current business banking call that Harrow & Vale can't share any information about another customer's account. That covers payment details, the meaning of a reference, the balance or ability to pay, and internal contacts. Point him to Haldane Homes directly for which invoice the £90 covered and for his overdue invoice, and to his own bank, Meridian, for the details of the £90 he received.

evidence.fact: The caller confirms he does not hold an account with Harrow & Vale; he banks with Meridian.

Haldane Homes Ltd is an H&V business customer. The caller is identified as a third party, not an H&V customer. The details visible in Haldane's account (a £90 Faster Payment and other payments to TILLEYS MAINTENANCE) belong to Haldane and are confidential to them.
The caller asks what the £90 reference means, whether Haldane can afford a £1,400 invoice, and for a direct number for Haldane's account contact.

conflicts: The caller assumes that because our customer paid him, the bank can discuss that payment with him (event-004). The bank's duty of confidentiality is to Haldane Homes Ltd, its customer (event-001), and the caller is not authorised on that account.

rejected_options.option: Explain the reference or say which invoice the £90 was for, using Haldane's account view
rejected_options.reason: This would disclose our customer's payment details to a third party who is not authorised on the account. The details of the payment he received are available from his own bank, Meridian, and the invoice it relates to from Haldane.

rejected_options.option: Say whether Haldane has the money to pay the £1,400 invoice
rejected_options.reason: This would disclose a customer's balance or creditworthiness to a third party. It is confidential and outside what the bank can share.

rejected_options.option: Give a direct number for Haldane's relationship manager or account contact
rejected_options.reason: Internal contact details for a customer's account are not shared with third parties. Any dispute over the invoice is between him and Haldane.
The caller is not a Harrow & Vale customer and has no secure portal. Telling Haldane would share nothing they need and isn't called for.

rejected_options.option: Check Haldane's records or escalate to a team
rejected_options.reason: No record check is needed to refuse disclosure, and looking further into the customer's account for a third party is not appropriate. Nothing suggests fraud or a complaint, so this is a routine confidentiality refusal.

input.final_result: Nothing about Haldane Homes Ltd's account has been disclosed to the caller. He is being told on the call that the bank can't discuss another customer's account. He is pointed to Haldane Homes for which invoice the payment was for and for his overdue invoice, and to Meridian for the details of the payment he received.
